name: Mongol Destruction of the Khwarazmian Empire
summary: Genghis Khan's invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire (1219–1221) was among the most destructive campaigns in history. Cities such as Bukhara, Samarkand, and Merv, then among the world's largest and most culturally advanced, were sacked, their populations massacred or enslaved. The irrigation systems that supported Central Asian agriculture were destroyed, and the region's demographic and cultural recovery took centuries.
outcomes: Irrigation systems destroyed; agricultural landscape wrecked
Central Asian civilization set back by generations

_quarry.structural_significance: The Mongol destruction of Khwarezm depopulated one of the most developed regions of the medieval world; it broke Central Asian Islamic civilization at its peak.
